en: Oṃ, salutation to the Supreme Śambhu! By whom the entire state of Śambhu is pervaded, the lineage of the Command (ājñākrama), which is always divine, semi-divine, and non-divine, moving in the void of space, the whirlwind, the abode of the universe;
having drunk the nectar of the rising moon, which is the mass of the bliss of gnosis and the dense [essence] of immortality, she sports.
In the worlds of the Sun, Moon, and Fire, Trottalā resides in the Ājñā-japa.
The illustrious Śrīkaṇṭhanātha said:
O Goddess, I have heard all of your eternal discourse;
yet even now, O Goddess, there remains a doubt regarding the determination of the Trotalā-krama.
The retention of the mantra is now described. Having risen in the morning...
The syllable *ū* is the seed-syllable of Vāyu; above that is Varuṇa, and upon him is Vajrapāṇi.
Above that is the supreme seed-syllable of Fire, joined with the final letter of the [vowel] series and accompanied by *haṃsa*.
It is marked by the moon and the bindu at its end, is seated upon a white lotus, and flows with streams of milk.
But one who has seen a falsehood constantly burns his family with evil that is indeed like Mount Meru.
Thus, one should meditate upon the *kuṭa* within one's own heart, resembling the sword of the Sun, for the destruction of evil.
One should perform a bath in water, or alternatively, the five-limbed ritual (pañcāṅga).

Having placed the seed-syllables of Earth (KṢOṂ), Water (VAṂ), Fire (RAṂ), and the Lord of Speech (VĀGĪŚA), joined with the Bindu, seven times into the water, one should then recite the Weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*) which proceeds from the three abodes of the jewels.

Alternatively, having washed the five limbs— the two hands, the two feet, and the face— one performs the mantra-bath through meditation on the jar-seal (*kumbha-mudrā*) and so forth, using a mantra devoid of the *astra* [mantra] and free from dust.
O best of practitioners, listen with one voice to that which is taught by all lineages for the sake of attaining the fruit of accomplishment:
virtuous ones obtain success only so long as the mantras, beginning with *praṇava* and ending with the rest, have not [been mastered].
The power previously indicated as named Kujā (Mars), conjoined with the cruel [planets], is the support for the letter Ā;
it is the foundation for maintenance and withdrawal.
Ambikā, mounted upon a serpent, with the mandalas of the secret power (guhyaśakti),
is that goddess who is remembered as the one who supports the back and has become the waters.
Then Kusumādevī is at Nāgasthā, along with the three maṇḍalas;
Śrīkarī is Tejabhūtā, while the third power is Raudriṇī.
The goddess Dīpanī, Śikhinī, Parāmbā, Karṇendu, Bindu, and Viśvahā—
when extracted in reverse order, she is the bestower of the power of moving through the sky (khecaratva).
The Haṃsa, honored for its grace, residing in the hearts of living beings,
extracted as the element of space, is nectar that bestows liberation.
As previously described, the excellent water-wheel is yellow and square, with white segments.
The fire-circle, possessing the quality of redness and divine, is the six-cornered wheel called Vāta, which is intensely smoky.
The entire universe, including the five elements that have arisen, along with calamities and mental afflictions, is equal to the pure sun;
we meditate upon Him who possesses a tranquil form of firm resolve, who has four arms, and who is seated upon a lotus.
With his right hand he holds a trident, and with the other [hand] he bestows gifts in due order;
in his left hands he displays the gestures of granting boons and fear; by means of the five-fold mantras, he [manifests] his hands, body, and faces.
The mantra consists of the elements beginning with Earth (Dharā) in sequence, with the number of repetitions for each being zero, two, one, and zero respectively;
when increasing by a hundred thousand, it amounts to exactly fifteen hundred thousand recitations, and at the conclusion, there should be an oblation of ten million offerings with clarified butter.
This Śrī Praṇaveśvara is the granter of desires, the remover of the suffering of his devotees, and the bestower of the worlds of virtue;
his state was attained at the conclusion of sacrifices and oblations by gods, lords of sages, humans, demons, and perfected beings.
Thus ends the exposition of the fivefold praṇava.
The fruit of eating sacrificial porridge.
Ākāśa is Sadāśiva; Ānanda. || 1 || Vāyu is Īśvara; Khecara. || 2 || Tejas is Rudra; Bhūcara. || 3 ||
Viṣṇu and water [are the offerings]—4. Earth, Brahmā, and the *sekharacaru*—5. The *sarvacaru*. All the gods contemplate the sky, the sesame seed, and likewise the manifested time.
At the primordial time, that which is in the form of food was consumed; it is the destroyer of impurity. 1.
Even for a killer of a mother, a killer of a father, a slayer of a Brahmin, or a stealer of a cow, all sins shall be destroyed by merely consuming the lamp. || 1 ||
From Garuḍa down to the Caṭaka bird, [the practitioner] is perceived as moving through the sky;
at the time of the festival, he consumes the wing, yet he does not see the supreme wing. || 2 ||
From the lion down to the goat, whatever creature is born from a womb, one should eat it during the auspicious festival times; such a being does not perceive the cycle of rebirth.
A fish lives in the water by means of its fins, tail, and other parts;
yet when it is caught at the time of the festival, though it is eaten, it does not see the water. || 4 ||
The road, the earth, the boat, the food, the house, and the mouth—these one should avoid at the time of the festival;
one should eat the boat-food, yet one does not see the boat. 5.
The life of one who eats [only] fruits and the like by means of the seed of taste is such that,
if he should eat the seed at the time of the festival, he does not see the seed of liberation.
O beloved, whatever is to be eaten or consumed has not attained the state of Brahman;
and whatever substance possesses flavor is established as Viṣṇu.
Having brought the three into a state of equal flavor, the Self-Existent One is the Great Lord, the enjoyer.
Worshipped by Varuṇa, the goddess is celebrated as Vāruṇī;
she is constantly drunk by the gods and is designated by the name Surā.
She who is eternally worshipped by Madana is proclaimed as Smadiretī;
she who has arisen in the ultimate reality is proclaimed as Parāśakti.
O beautiful one, starting from the root of the tongue and extending to the heart,
the region of sixteen finger-breadths should be known as the place of the nectar of self-savoring (svādāmṛta).
It is endowed with sixteen attendant digits and is sixteen finger-breadths in length.
O Goddess, O Divine One, you who are the embodiment of nectar, drink the intoxicating [essence].
First, Vahni drinks; second, he drinks with Śaśin;
third, Viṣṇu drinks; and fourth, Varuṇa drinks.
The fifth [cup] the goddesses should drink; the sixth, Vaśavartin;
the seventh, the Ṛṣis; and the eighth, Sarvagaṇeśa, should drink.
The ninth [was given] by Dharmarāja, and the tenth by Maruta.
O Dear One, the son of Brahmā should drink [the nectar] in the eleventh position.
One should worship Kubera on the twelfth day, Vaināyaka on the thirteenth,
Paśupati on the fourteenth, and Prajāpati on the full moon day.
Having drunk these five, one should manifest the sixteen-fold [state] under control;
O auspicious lady, this has not been drunk by humans, but having drunk it, it belongs to those who have attained Śambhu.
And having drunk what was spoken, O blessed one, now listen to the god:
she who is Rāśā is the goddess Umā, and he who is Madya is Maheśvara.
He who is Brahmā himself in his form, O Janārdana, is the possessor of yoga;
he whose essence is Soma is himself the impetus and the purifier of that impetus.
O Goddess, O Sovereign of the Gods, I shall now describe to you the dissolution of knowledge and discernment; listen attentively to me now.
First they dissolve at the tip of the tongue, immediately thereafter at the tip of the nose;
the third is at the end of the uvula, and for the fourth, one should place them between the eyebrows.

The fifth [syllable] is in the place of the crest-lock, and the sixth at the end of the crest-lock. Resembling an *atasī* flower, the partless radiance dissolves into the middle place; O Goddess, this must be understood with diligent effort.
Aiṃ 5. The goddess Lākṣārasaṇībhā possesses a radiance equal to a ruby;
she is a singer with the form of a youthful maiden, possessing three eyes and a divine appearance.
O Maṇḍirānanda, O Consciousness, bearing eighteen arms,
holding a sword, a trident, the gesture of granting boons, a mace, a hand-drum, and a hammer.
She shines with a mace and a lotus held in her right hands,
while her left hands hold a water-pot, a small sword, a goad, a bell, a skull-cup, a khaṭvāṅga, a conch, a blue lotus, and the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya), ending with the bindu.
Adorned with the majesty of divine jewels and golden ornaments, seated upon a lotus-throne, he is established in the posture of the lotus-seat.
Thus Vāruṇī, possessing a divine form, [approached] the great god Mahādeva.
One should not impart the essential core of the *Kaulika* tradition to one who is greedy, deceitful, cruel, or possessed by hypocrisy, envy, and pride;
nor especially to those who revile their guru.
He who is always devoted to the service of his gurus, who is fond of the *samayas*,
and who has been tested for a year— he too, O illustrious lady,
shall grant the *pañcacakra* of the Supreme Goddess.

Śambhu, the mind-born, residing within the intellect at the end [of the path], is seen in his own abode of the heart as a peak formed by the elements of water (rasa), touch (sparśa), fire (agni), and the syllable *marmmāli*;
rising upward like a mass of many great sunbeams, he is the destroyer of dread.
The King of Mantras, Śrī-Śāmbhava, which bestows the fortune of liberation upon living beings.
One should join the fire (Ra) below the moving [letter] (Ca), and the pervasive unborn (Ha) above the four vowels;
one should place the half-measure in the middle. This is declared as the two kinds of Saṃkūṭa.
The Śāmbhava, known as the King of Mantras, bestows nectar;
the Āṇaveśa, situated in the midst of the measurement, grants the perfection of the pinnacle of realized knowledge.
In the division beginning with *ka*, situated above the moving [center], it bestows both enjoyment and liberation;
I shall explain that which consists of eighty-one parts, exactly as it has come from the mouth of the Guru.
The earth, water, great fire, wind, and space— along with their respective elements— when consumed by the flames of the world-destroying dissolution,
reach a state of total integration as a single mass;
yet even that is shattered by the power of the Vedic melody, becoming silent, radiant, and partless.
Śiva is beyond the reach of another's intellect; He is the mere source of existence, while heaven is empty [of Him].
Thus ends the section on the ninefold self-gateways.
The Goddess who is the authority for the five groups, adorned with thirty-two syllables,
is the Vidyā Kujeśvarī, who removes the grasping of the delusion of existence for those destined for liberation.
I shall explain that unblemished [mantra] as it was heard from the venerable Guru:
the final seed-syllable of the dental class (*ta-varga*), joined with *kānvayā* (***).
The terrifying Śivā, likewise Khaḍgaṅgārā joined with Sūkṣma;
likewise Śrutipraṇava, and Krodha joined with the fifth, surrounded.
Nalinī and Kaṅkaṭā are pierced by Āśvareṇa;
likewise Cala, Sūkṣmasamākrānta, Śikhā, and Svacchandaka.

One should extract the last letter of the ka-group as the seed-syllable, followed by the letter preceding ḍha (i.e., ṭa), which is preceded by the first vowel (a) and conjoined with the letter following ṣma (i.e., ra). This is the syllable *kāla* (kra). It is then to be conjoined with the letter following *bhṛṅgha* (i.e., *ṣma*). Thus, one should extract [the mantra] beginning with a vowel.
Then, having extracted the fourth letter of the *ka*-group joined with [the vowel] *u*,
and then the fifth *dīpa* [vowel], one worships Mahākālī, who is honored by me and the gods.
May [the Lord] together with Queen Māyā protect us from the four [directions];
may Ananta, joined with Kūrma and Aja, and united with Krūra, protect us.
Again, having extracted [the seed-syllable] that is immediately followed by the secret power (guhyaśakti),
and [the syllable] Kaṅkaṭa joined with Umākānta and Māyā in a subtle manner.
Having extracted the repetition and the hatred, Chāgala [extracted] that which is joined with Māyā;
having extracted Cāmuṇḍā by means of Kūrma, she was pierced by Jhaṇṭhīśa.
This goddess Śrī Samayā is obtained from the mouth of the Guru;
by the mere recollection of her, the three worlds are said to be [subjugated].
Whether in one's own body or in another's body, regarding things spoken or unspoken,
he who worships Kubjīśānī finds no sin.
Furthermore, he whose nature is pure being who worships the Mistress of the Kula known as Samaya— that object for which one strives is not accomplished.

He who recites the sequence of syllables and non-syllables one hundred thousand times, having exhausted [all bonds], becomes equal in qualities to Kubjīśa; he is himself the Lord, the creator and the destroyer.
This king is endowed with the fruits of hundreds of millions of mantras followed by those belonging to the six stages of life; therefore, this speech has arisen from his island-like [virtue].
Thus ends the section on the door according to the *samaya*.
Oṃ, salutations to Tripurā! The extraction of the mantra is now described.
Below that is the power of Mādana; at its end is the garland of bindus.
From the seed-syllable of space (Ē) comes the syllable of fire (Ra) situated below it.
O Goddess, this Vāgbhava [Bīja], joined with Māyā, Vid, and Īśvara, and placed above all, is the one that sets in motion the sovereignty of speech. || 1 ||
Having uttered the seed-syllable of Śiva three times according to the sequence of emanation, maintenance, and dissolution—
at the beginning, middle, and end— the first two [syllables] are devoid of the first [mantra].
With the first letter, one should place the letter of Madana below the first;
one should join the seed-syllable of Indra situated beneath Mavāsthitiśiva.
Likewise, O Maheśvarī, even below Layashiva,
it is joined with Māyā, Vidya, and Īśvara, and adorned with a half-moon.
Thus it is: this great seed-syllable is the king of desire and brings about great prosperity. || 2 ||
O Great Goddess, one should extract the seed-syllable of Māyā joined with the intoxicant [Ra] and the vowel of Śakra [U],
as well as the seed-syllable of the Moon [Sa] alone, which is the seed-syllable of Śakti.
Having abandoned the sequence of emanation, the Goddess [performs] the prior utterance in due order;
thus is this Great Goddess Mahātripurasundarī. (3)
The extraction of the mantra of Tripurā is the Turīya-vidyā.
The mantra for the northern direction is recited here.

May this speech of Bhava always be victorious— she who grants the fulfillment of all desires, who has entered the ocean of worldly existence, who is the supreme state of being, the destroyer of all afflictions, the auspicious one,
who holds a water-pot as worn by Śarva, and who bestows the perfection of bliss.
The supreme, stainless Śrī Siddhalakṣmī, the highest glory, bestows auspiciousness upon the Arūpya realm.
Māyābīja, the supreme essence of the lineage (kulamāyā), Mālinī, Mādāmātre, Maheśvarī, she who wears a garland of pearls in the family of Mi,
whose eyes are jewels of the perfection of *māyā*, whose heart is pride, and who is the eight-footed Yoga.
She bestows the fulfillment of one's desires in the heart of that person who is devoted to the propitiation of the mantra.
The illustrious one does not shine like a fragment of the moon; she is the stainless Śrī, the bestower of peace in the corners,
the universal soul, the sole mother of the universe who consists of the awakening of the states of waking and so forth,
and she sprinkles the multitude of arrows with the flowing water of the nectar of compassion.
Victorious is Kālī, the deceiver of the seasons, who bestows the arrows of the cycle of rebirth.
[The Hymn on the Extraction of the Śrī Siddhilakṣmī Mantra is completed.]
